title: Job scheduler
description:
A printer receives jobs with a priority from 1 (low) to 9 (urgent). It always prints the most urgent job next. Among jobs of **equal** priority it prints them in the order they were submitted.

Write `std::vector<std::string> printOrder(const std::vector<Job>& jobs)` returning the job names in the order they are printed. `jobs` is given in submission order.

Use a `std::priority_queue`. On its own it does not promise any order among equal priorities, so store something extra alongside each job that breaks ties the right way (the position it was submitted at works), and give the queue a comparison that looks at both.
hints: Push `(priority, position)` pairs, or a small struct, with the job's index as the position. The queue must put a higher priority first and, for equal priorities, a **smaller** position first.
Give `std::priority_queue` a comparison lambda that returns true when the first element should come out **later**: lower priority, or equal priority and larger position.
